title: ‘The Debut’: Jesse Eisenberg Praises Oscar Frontrunner Julianne Moore’s ‘Perfect Performance’ at NYFF
description: You couldn’t imagine a more ideal setting for “The Debut” than Alice Tully Hall on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, where it had its New York premi
body:
You couldn’t imagine a more ideal setting for “The Debut” than Alice Tully Hall on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, where it had its New York premiere Wednesday evening as part of the New York Film Festival.

	The third feature film from writer-director Jesse Eisenberg, and follow-up to his Oscar-winning “A Real Pain,” is set in 1990 and follows Mona Friedman (Julianne Moore), a timid, browbeaten housewife in Central Jersey who disrupts her mind-numbing routine by auditioning for the role of the janitor in a community theater production of the musical “Nosy Neighbors.” There, she finds community among her castmates (Halle Bailey and Colton Ryan among them) and clashes with her imperious director (the inimitable Paul Giamatti), as she falls deeper and deeper into character. Eisenberg’s film garnered considerable laughs — and applause — from the theater-going crowd at its starry NYFF screening that saw Eisenberg, the cast, producer Emma Stone and even Claire Danes in attendance.
	

	Eisenberg was born in Queens and grew up in East Brunswick, New Jersey, and said during a post-screening Q&A that he modeled Mona’s journey after “the community that I found” doing local theater, where “the shows were always secondary to the backstage family.”


	“I’ve done community theater where the talent is just as good as Broadway talent, but they don’t feel this personal ambition to be center stage,” he explained, making it “so much sweeter than what we do.”

	But Eisenberg confessed that the “tonally odd” film is, first and foremost, a monument to Moore, who also starred in Eisenberg’s directorial debut. He wrote the role specifically for her and sang the Oscar-winning actress’s praises to the New York crowd.
	

	“If you didn’t know that beforehand, I imagine you can tell that now,” he offered. “Has there ever been a more perfect performance?”

	Moore, who is getting plenty of Oscar buzz for her no-holds-barred performance, said she wanted to do another musical after “Dear Evan Hansen,” an experience she “loved” because it was “scary and fun.” She also was attracted to the script and the idea of inhabiting Eisenberg.

	“I am in effect his avatar, and the fact that he put his experience in a middle-aged woman’s body is extraordinary,” Moore attested.

	She continued: “This is a person who doesn’t feel like they fit into their life and is on the brink of change… What does it mean to step into something just because you have this desire? And where do you go from there?”

	Moore said that Eisenberg’s script made Mona relatable to everyone since it “actualized this very human feeling of wanting something and not knowing what it is.”

schema.headline: ‘The Debut’: Jesse Eisenberg Praises Oscar Frontrunner Julianne Moore’s ‘Perfect Performance’ at NYFF

title: Danny and Oxide Pang’s Josie Ho-Starring Supernatural Thriller ‘The Mage’ Sets Busan Market Debut With Abnormal Studios (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Danny and Oxide Pang’s supernatural crime thriller “The Mage,” starring Josie Ho, is being introduced to international buyers at the Busan Internati
body:
Danny and Oxide Pang’s supernatural crime thriller “The Mage,” starring Josie Ho, is being introduced to international buyers at the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) as the film opens in its first Asian territories.

	Southeast Asian distributor Abnormal Studios will meet with buyers at the market and connect interested parties with 852 Films, which produced the title and will take charge of subsequent sales inquiries and rights deals for territories that remain open.
	

	Conroy Chan produced the Cantonese-language feature for 852 Films, which sees the Pang Brothers once again sharing directing duties. The pair are known internationally for genre fare such as “The Eye,” “Bangkok Dangerous” and “Re-Cycle.”


	Ho plays Lan Pui Ching, a one-time spirit medium turned scavenger who gathers cast-off objects she is convinced hold the spirits of those who met sudden deaths, and who tries to guide those souls toward reincarnation. She keeps turning up at the scenes of deaths that look suspicious, which puts her on the radar of police officer Wong Ming. As the investigation uncovers a string of killings linked to a strange ritual, the two are pushed into working together, facing down otherworldly threats as well as unfinished business from Lan’s past.

	Iman Taheri, Carlos Chan, German Cheung, Kathy Yuen and Sabrina Ng round out the cast. The film fuses horror and crime with Hong Kong spiritual folklore, and is aimed at fans of midnight movies and cult cinema.

	“The Mage” world premiered in July at South Korea’s Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival (BIFAN). It then opened the Midnight section of the Bangkok International Film Festival and is set for its European premiere in the Sitges Collection strand at Spain’s Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival. Ho, who co-founded 852 Films, picked up the Fantastic Icon Award at BIFAN’s 30th edition, honoring her body of work in genre film.
	

	Two Asian deals are already in place. Edko Films took Hong Kong and Macau, and CJ ENM Hong Kong has Taiwan and Southeast Asia. The film opened in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Taiwan on Oct. 8, with Singapore to follow on Oct. 15 and Thailand on Oct. 29. Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam are due in November.

	Abnormal Studios, a subsidiary of Westec Media Limited, has been acquiring and releasing films since 2020 across Southeast Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Taiwan, Mongolia and Nepal, among other markets. Its releases include hits “How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies” and “Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In.” The company has handled more than 400 titles to date and now takes around 100 films to market each year.

schema.headline: Danny and Oxide Pang’s Josie Ho-Starring Supernatural Thriller ‘The Mage’ Sets Busan Market Debut With Abnormal Studios (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Nana Patekar, Indian Star of ‘Parinda’ and ‘Krantiveer,’ Dies at 75
description: Nana Patekar, the Indian Hindi and Marathi cinema actor whose roles ranged from the menacing crime lord of “Parinda” to the comic gangster of “Welco
body:
Nana Patekar, the Indian Hindi and Marathi cinema actor whose roles ranged from the menacing crime lord of “Parinda” to the comic gangster of “Welcome,” died Oct. 8, at his residence in Goa. He was 75.

	Patekar went into cardiac arrest at home and was declared dead at 5:20 am local time, news agency ANI reported. “Despite 45 minutes of continuous CPR, he could not be revived,” Dr. Shekhar Salkar, chief of the oncology department at Manipal Hospital, told ANI. Salkar said a medico-legal case had been opened and an autopsy would follow.
	

	Born Vishwanath Patekar in Murud-Janjira, in what is now in the western Indian state of Maharashtra’s Raigad district, he studied at Mumbai’s Sir J.J. Institute of Applied Art. His first stage role came under director Vijaya Mehta. He made his film debut in “Gaman” in 1978 and spent the following decade in smaller Marathi and Hindi parts, including a role in Mira Nair’s Oscar-nominated “Salaam Bombay!” (1988).


	His breakthrough came with “Parinda” (1989), in which he played a crime lord. The role brought him an Indian National Film Award for best supporting actor and the Filmfare award in the same category. Patekar also directed “Prahaar: The Final Attack” (1991), starring alongside Madhuri Dixit, and went through army training to prepare for his officer role.

	“Krantiveer” (1994), in which he played a disgraced gambler who ends up rallying ordinary people to fight back, won him the Indian National Film Award for best actor along with Filmfare and Screen awards. A second National Award for supporting actor followed for “Agni Sakshi” (1996). The same year he played the deaf parent of Manisha Koirala in “Khamoshi: The Musical.”
	

	He also took Filmfare’s best villain prize twice, for “Angaar” (1992) and “Apaharan” (2005). Only he and Irrfan Khan won Filmfare trophies as lead, supporting player and villain.

	In the 2000s he played a police encounter specialist in “Ab Tak Chhappan” (2004) and a taxi driver opposite John Abraham in “Taxi No. 9211” (2006). With “Welcome” (2007), in which he played Uday Shetty, a mob boss with thwarted movie-star ambitions, he found a new audience, and he returned to the part in “Welcome Back” (2015). He played a politician in “Raajneeti” (2010).

	In Marathi cinema, he won Filmfare Marathi best actor awards for “Dr. Prakash Baba Amte – The Real Hero” (2014) and “Natsamrat” (2016), in which he starred as an aging theater veteran. He was the Hindi voice of Shere Khan in “The Jungle Book” (2016) and appeared opposite Rajinikanth in the Tamil film “Kaala” (2018).

	Later credits included “The Vaccine War” (2023), “Vanvaas” (2024) and “Housefull 5” (2025). This year he starred in series “Sankalp” on Amazon MX Player and appeared alongside Shahid Kapoor in “O’Romeo.”

	Patekar received the Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian honor, in 2013. He was commissioned into the Territorial Army in 1988 with the rank of captain. During the 1999 Kargil conflict he was posted with the Maratha Light Infantry, holding the rank of major, and had risen to lieutenant colonel by the time he left in 2013. In 2015 he launched the Naam Foundation alongside Makarand Anaspure to support Maharashtra farmers hit by drought.

	His later years were also marked by controversy. Actor Tanushree Dutta accused him in 2008 of harassing her on the set of “Horn ‘Ok’ Pleassss,” and she repeated the allegation in 2018. Her accusations helped spark the #MeToo movement in the Hindi film industry. Mumbai police registered a case against Patekar and three others in October 2018 but filed a closure report in June 2019. Patekar consistently denied the allegations.

schema.headline: Nana Patekar, Indian Star of ‘Parinda’ and ‘Krantiveer,’ Dies at 75

title: Sebastian Stan Doesn’t Know How ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Turned Out, But Says It’s ‘Probably Heartbreaking’: ‘We’ll See Who Makes It’
description: Sebastian Stan, who suited back up as the Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes, for the forthcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” recently revealed he hasn’t actual
body:
Sebastian Stan, who suited back up as the Winter Soldier, Bucky Barnes, for the forthcoming “Avengers: Doomsday,” recently revealed he hasn’t actually seen the movie yet — but expects it to be “heartbreaking.”

	“I haven’t seen the movie, and I don’t know how it turned out,” the actor admitted while speaking with Decider. “I’m sure it’s going to be probably heartbreaking, in a lot of ways. We’ll see who makes it to the next level.”
	

	Stan did say he got to “reunite with everyone” on set, adding, “It was very nostalgic to look back and think about all of these years that we’ve known each other and grew up together. It’s incredible in that way,” he said. “It’s been a family, and it never stops being that way.”


	While fans have interpreted Stan’s comments as a tip that more than a few of the beloved characters will be killed off in the “Avengers: Endgame” follow-up, the actor is the latest “Doomsday” cast member to confess that they don’t really know what to expect when it comes to the film’s narrative. Recently, Alan Cumming, who will reprise his role as the mutant superhero Nightcrawler, told SiriusXM: “To be honest, I don’t fully understand the plot.” (He first appeared as the character in 2003’s “X2: X-Men United.”) Cumming also noted that most of his scenes were shot “in front of a blue screen.”

	Perhaps the confusion stems from the unfinished script the co-directors, Joe and Anthony Russo, shot the film with. “We always view the script as a living organism,” Joe told the Associated Press last month. “We’re improvisation-based, rehearsal-based directors. We like to see what the actors bring to the characters, and sometimes you don’t get the actors until a few days or few weeks before you shoot them. And a lot of the time, that’s when the magic happens.”
	

	Stan first appeared in “Captain America: The First Avenger” in 2011, going on to appear in “Captain America: The Winter Soldier,” “Captain America: Civil War,” “Avengers: Infinity War,” and more Marvel films. 

	“Fjord,” the actor’s latest film, hits theaters Friday. “Avengers: Doomsday” will premiere theatrically on Dec. 18.

schema.headline: Sebastian Stan Doesn’t Know How ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Turned Out, But Says It’s ‘Probably Heartbreaking’: ‘We’ll See Who Makes It’

title: Patreon Co-founder Sam Yam Partners with Podcaster Chloe Shih After Joining OpenAI’s Creator Initiative (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Patreon co-founder Sam Yam joined OpenAI last month to lead its creator initiative — and he’s already got his first project set up.

	Yam is partner
body:
Patreon co-founder Sam Yam joined OpenAI last month to lead its creator initiative — and he’s already got his first project set up.

	Yam is partnering with podcast host Chloe Shih, who launched her podcast “Office Drama” earlier this year, on a new series to explore how technology can help those navigating parenthood and the first years of a child’s education. The series, the specifics of which the company has not disclosed, hopes to showcase how AI’s development can help families, in line with Yam’s intention upon hiring to help creators “shape culture” and “unite diverse communities together.”
	

	“Being a parent is becoming increasingly expensive and even out of reach for many who are already trying to balance their professional and personal lives,” said Shih, who’s expecting a child, in a statement. “I’ve often seen tech products focusing too much on convenience and not enough on addressing actual problems that the everyday person faces, and I want to make sure we build for people outside the tech bubble, too.”


	Shih will also use OpenAI’s Dots, its always-on AI agent and competitor to Meta’s Muse that it unveiled during its DevDay showcase last month, to help produce the project.

	Yam, who co-founded Patreon as a creator-focused monetization platform in 2013 and served as its president, announced on X last month that he would join OpenAI as its head of creator product — and that Patreon’s heads of product and engineering would join him. The exits followed Patreon’s layoffs in July, when it pink-slipped roughly 20% of its staff.
	

	Yam wrote in a Sept. 22 X thread that he loved creators’ “relentless dedication to the craft” and was excited to help them bring “many more of their ideas to life.”

	“I believe human creativity is paramount,” he wrote. “It allows us to see ourselves reflected in the world around us and drives authentic connections — and at the heart of it is a universal desire to be seen as we are and know that we are not alone.”

	OpenAI‘s embrace of creators was made clear earlier this year when it poached Charles Porch, who connected celebrities to Instagram and helped them use the platform to bolster their careers, from Meta earlier this year. Some of those efforts have landed participating creators in hot water, however, including a maligned creators’ trip OpenAI organized in August to Wildflower Farms, a luxury estate in New York’s Hudson Valley.

schema.headline: Patreon Co-founder Sam Yam Partners with Podcaster Chloe Shih After Joining OpenAI’s Creator Initiative (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Questlove Reflects on the Power of Vulnerability and Being a Trailblazer: ‘I Gotta Be the Change I Want to Be’
description:
More than 30 years into his career, Questlove is still open to change.

	The Roots frontman and multi-hyphenate has performed in Jimmy Fallon’s in-h
body:
More than 30 years into his career, Questlove is still open to change.

	The Roots frontman and multi-hyphenate has performed in Jimmy Fallon’s in-house band for over a decade, was a producer on the “Hamilton” cast album, is an adjunct professor at NYU, hosts a podcast and has written eight books.

	Since 2020, Questlove has also directed four documentaries. It was that endeavor that he was initially most opposed to: “I had to do a lot of work to realize that — I know it’s cliché — I gotta be the change I want to be.”
	

	Questlove sat down with Variety‘s Jem Aswad to discuss embracing vulnerability and being a changemaker at the Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage presented by OUTFRONT.

	Questlove said he would have called Prince his North Star when he first entered the industry. Now, with the “residue” of his Earth, Wind & Fire documentary still lingering, he said he feels like a new artist. “I’m still learning what the Questlove brand is,” he said. “I joke that this is Questlove 3.0 happening right now.”

	“Earth, Wind & Fire (To Be Celestial vs That’s the Weight of the World)” was released in June. Directed and produced by Questlove, the documentary explores the band’s career and that of its founder, Maurice White. While creating the documentary, he read many of the books White read during the band’s genesis, which inspired his current approach to creativity.

	Questlove recalled the “too cool for school” attitude he saw in artists like Miles Davis and his own mindset on his records as protecting vulnerability. “We see it in our politics. We see it in our creativity,” he said. “We’re going to implode as a world if we don’t learn what emotions are and how we can use our vulnerability.”
	

	Questlove’s first documentary project, “Summer of Soul (…or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised),” about the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival, came out in 2021. “You can’t discount the timing of everything,” he said of the film’s arrival after the initial lockdown and protests following the murder of George Floyd. He said people saw the film because they were curious, but “they didn’t realize how important it was to celebrate joy.”

	His next project, “Sly Lives! (aka The Burden of Black Genius),” focused more on the tendency he noticed in Black creatives to self-sabotage after becoming successful. Then came the Earth, Wind & Fire documentary, which he made because he “wanted to make a film that lets us focus on our dreams.”

	Still, Questlove didn’t think he was the right person for the job of documentarian prior to “Summer of Soul.” “I didn’t know I was a storyteller,” he said. “I’m out there like, ‘Well, search for a real storyteller,’ and they’re like, ‘Dude, you’re that storyteller.’ Once I realized it, it became a passion.” He described himself as someone who will use history to attract audiences, but will put things in his films to make the audience reckon with their present.

	While he has ventured into filmmaking, Questlove has not left music behind. The Roots Picnic held its 18th iteration this May, headlined by Jay-Z. The festival has grown, but “we’re not just rubber-stamping,” he said. “We are curating the festival. We’re playing with some of the acts, and people really feel like a community.”

	On “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon,” The Roots serve as — among other things — the live walk-up music for guests. Some celebrities send requests for their entrance song, but Questlove said, “the magic of the show is what I choose your walk-on song.”

	The best thing about “The Tonight Show,” Questlove said, is that it allows the band members to be present with their families. “The Beatles broke up after seven years, and we’re going on year 35 and we’re still like the best of friends,” he said. “We’re still as silly as we were in high school, and still fun. If you’re not friends with your partners, then all this is for naught.”

schema.headline: Questlove Reflects on the Power of Vulnerability and Being a Trailblazer: ‘I Gotta Be the Change I Want to Be’

title: Hayley Williams Proves There’s a Lot More to Her Than Paramore in a Galvanizing Solo Show at the Hollywood Bowl: Concert Review
description:
Oct 7, 2026 8:09pm PT	
	

	
		Hayley Williams Proves There’s a Lot More to Her Than Paramore in a Galvanizing Solo Show at the Holly
body:
Oct 7, 2026 8:09pm PT	
	

	
		Hayley Williams Proves There’s a Lot More to Her Than Paramore in a Galvanizing Solo Show at the Hollywood Bowl: Concert Review
	
	
			


			
			
	

	

		
	
				

	When do trimmings become the main course? Or, to pose it in employment terms: When does a side hustle became the real hustle? And can that just go down without a hitch?

	These are just ways into trying to think about developments in the career of Hayley Williams, who easily sold out two shows this week at the Hollywood Bowl, something we wouldn’t necessarily have taken for granted for her as a solo artist even a couple of years ago. In the first of two nights there Monday, Williams performed for almost exactly two hours without doing a single Paramore song — and what’s remarkable is, nobody cared.

	Well, maybe that’s an overstatement: Probably someone out there in the full house of 17,000 had read the promo material for the tour and figured the promise of material from her three solo albums “plus exciting surprises” at least left room for the possibility of a Paramore or tune or two. But the “exciting surprises” on Monday amounted to a Portishead cover and a surprise encore appearance by Zedd, as opposed to “That’s What You Get.” Which was fine. More than fine, really: Williams’ Bowl set made for one of the most satisfying rock shows you could see this year, regardless of the fact that the only misery business being transacted was the unusually sweltering October weather that had everyone present walking up in a sweat.

	Speaking of boiling, this all boils down to: What a difference a single album can make. For Williams, that album was 2025’s “Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party,” which she originally dribbled out in mysterious spurts like it was a bunch of between-project demos before everyone gradually realized that it added up to the game-changer project of her career. Five months ago or so, she did a tour of small theaters (see Variety‘s review of her May L.A. show at the Wiltern) in which the setlist consisted primary of all 20 tracks from “Ego Death,” plus an excerpt of “Please Don’t Let Me Be Misunderstood” as a bonus mission statement. For anyone who caught that mini-tour, which felt surprisingly closer to a full meal than a teaser, it’s no surprise that this current fall amphitheater run feels like a decent summation of a long-building repertoire, rather than the shorter sliver of her life’s work to date that she’s actually offering.



	

					Hayley Williams at the Hollywood Bowl, Oct. 5, 2026
									Zachary Gray
	



	Part of the pleasure Williams is clearly taking in this current outing is that she’s getting to tour behind two albums at once — not just “Ego Death,” which she’s now doing 12 tracks from, but a good 10 from “Petals for Armor,” the 2020 album that she’d planned to follow up wih a debut solo tour before the pandemic changed plans. Perhaps it shouldn’t be a huge shock that, in contrast, she only picked one selection from the album that came between these two, 2021’s “Flowers for Vases/Descansos,” an album so flagrantly somber it felt like a side project among side projects. But the one “Vases” song that did get performed, “Just a Lover,” got an interesting spot — or spots, since solemn excerpts from it were played by her at the piano to open the show and then be reprised at the close of the main set, perhaps as a reminder of how un-perky her music could be if she let more depressing thoughts take over. (One of the despondent lines from that song, “No more music for the masses,” was emblazoned on one of the shirts sold at the merch stand, proving that the singer maintains a fine-tuned sense of irony.)



	Williams can be plenty downbeat, lyrically, at least, even when she’s keeping those other “Flowers for Vases” songs locked in the closet. And it was telling, in some way, that the one cover song she has added to this tour is Portishead’s “Wandering Star,” which is literally the farthest thing from sunny, with its grief-stricken verses and “The blackness of darkness forever” refrain — performed with Williams hovering over an old-school-looking computer bank to produce those sounds, as seen in a direct-overhead shot on the Bowl’s big screens. She did mean to take a bit to get the party started, as that descent into celestial bleakness was only the third song in the set. But then the cheerful “Hayley Williams Show” logo appeared on screen, as if we had just passed through an extended pre-credits sequence. “Simmer,” a “Petals” song that is one of her most emotional and vivid, followed, with its message that one way out from a traumatic relationship is to embrace a righteous rage.



	

					Hayley Williams at the Hollywood Bowl, Oct. 5, 2026
									Zachary Gray
	



	Williams took till the sixth song, “Ice in My OJ,” to finally broach the “Ego Death” album and some of its less soul-scouring material. (The song’s already ambiguous “I’m in a band!” chant takes on further layers, now that she’s out on the road with a pretty great assembly of musicians, that isn’t Paramore.) “Kill Me” quickly followed as one of her best current anthemic singalongs — not as nihilistic as it sounds, so much as just having some playful, emotionally exhausted fun twisting around Nietzsche’s overquoted words. “Hard” followed — her brutally honest look at the baggage around the feminine mystique, and the no-win situations that come with being a Woman in Rock. “My Friend” found her putting on a mask, literally, as a makeup person came out to affix glitter and paint around her eyes, as seen in extreme camera closeups, allowing her to look Mardi Gras-ready for the rest of the night, even if the actual party on stage had its emo ebbs and flows.



	

					Hayley Williams with string quartet at the Hollywood Bowl, Oct. 5, 2026
									Zachary Gray
	



	The poignant “Leave It Alone” saw the arrival of a female string quartet that periodically reappeared throughout the set — and also the intriguing use of a polyrhythm complex enough that you had to remind yourself it was your mind that was out of time, not the band itself. After this, Williams took time out between songs to celebrate the audience’s approval of all the “Petals for Amor” songs, like “Leave It Alone,” that had provided the majority of the set thus far, half-seriously remarking that the whole tour was a “Trojan horse” to get to finally play that material.


	Among the “Petals for Armor” songs in the set that were performed without comment: “Dead Horse,” a song understood to be about her relationship with former husband Chad Gilbert. As fans had noted, she took it out of the set for three concerts following his death last month, apparently out of respect, but it’s back in, because history is history, and relational trauma transformed into a sing-along dance track is always a recipe for concert success.

	Truth be told, as much cathartic fun as “Dead Horse” is — tempered by recent events or otherwise — there’s not a track on her more recent record that doesn’t beat it. And the second half of the show really soared as she uppped the “Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party” quotient, including the title track, which had footage of Nashville’s Lower Broadway logjams projected onto not just the stage but the Bowl’s entire proscenium. “Turns out he’s the least of our problems in Nashville,” she quipped, apparently referring to Morgan Wallen, the presumed “racist country singer” whose bar she visits in the tune, without expounding on who or what is even worse. “God bless Dolly Parton,” she added, bringing up a more universally beloved ambassador from her home state.



	Earlier, she’d gotten as political as she was going to during “Ice in My OJ,” popping in between lines to exclaim “Fuck ICE!” and “Free Palestine,” as is her nightly custom. (She expounded a bit more in her Instagram account earlier Monday. There’d been some news pickup of her “Fuck ICE” commentary at an earlier show, to which the White House officially responded, “America is grateful all the time for our federal law enforcement officers who keep us safe. We suggest Ms. Williams to (sic) thank them for their service, not belittle their sacrifice.” The singer replied to the presidents team on IG: “And may I suggest all Nazi bitches suck on my fat dick.”)

	Sadly, nothing she had to say at the Bowl was quite as colorful as what she has told the Trump administration on social media. But she did introduce “True Believer,” the recent song where she reckons with her own Southern heritage, the way she does each night on tour, saying: “The biggest threat to American democracy is Christian nationalism.” This standout number was conceived and is performed as a broadside against the hypocrisy she has spoken about growing up around in Tennessee; buried within it, plaintively, is a very sad gospel song.



	

					Hayley Williams at the Hollywood Bowl, Oct. 5, 2026
									Zachary Gray
	



	Williams was definitely letting her ex-vangelical freak flag fly on Monday night. She performed in a white mini-dress adorned by six apparently hand-drawn devil faces on the front, and a bigger and more sketched-in devil’s head on the back… all just above the cross inked on her upper thigh. At the end of her solo-piano cover of the Nina Simone/Animals classic “Don’t Let Me Be Misunderstood,” she put her hands to her head and used her fingers to form devil horns, which were writ large onto a background screen by a spotlight in the foreground making a silhouette. She won’t be the last church kid to be working out some issues literally in a spotlight.

	Does she count as a punk? The question arose in my mind the other week just because she used a statement she issued after her ex-husband’s death to thank him for helping introduce her to the hardcore scene, back when she was a teenager. Now, although pop-punk has been a reasonable loose description for some of Paramore’s music in the past, “hardcore” is not how you’d likely think of her distinctly melodic and flavorful music, then or now. But seeing her in action (or reading her in action, when she’s taking on Trump’s people), the influence is very much discernible, in her attitude. From her homemade dress to her literal stance on stage, Williams is a rock ‘n’ roller, regardless of what style of music she’s exploring in a particular song —  even the nostalgic bubblegum of the night’s penultimate number, her and Zedd’s 2013 collaboration “Stay the Night,” a reminder of a time when her fangs were a little more hidden. 

	(If we want to use punk-rock purely as a term of endearment, there is something of a punk ethos to Williams’ commitment to keeping tickets relatively low-priced and difficult to scalp, too, via the Face Value program. Even though tickets immediately sold out months ago, most of the good ones coming in around a reasonable $130, on the day of the show it was easy to find some resale tickets at that same value, due to the measures put in place, which ultimately contributed to the feel-good quality of the gig.)


	After her aside with Zedd, Williams brought things back to the now with the nightly closer, one of the best songs from “Ego Death,” “Parachute,” one of those numbers that manages to sound ecstatic and defeated at the same time, with its “I thought you were gonna catch me!” chorus. Is she singing to a friend in that song? Or maybe to Mirtazapine (the subject of another great encore inclusion)? Even a favorite med can let you down.
	

	That finale number had a tinge of hard-earned bitterness, but at the same time, it’s really a glorification of hard-earned self-sufficiency. Which is not a bad message to send a crowd of mostly young people out with… and a little bit appropriate for the state of her own career, where suddenly she is… bigger than Paramore? Is that possible? Maybe not, in the most realistic sense. But you do get the feeling that, with her first two solo albums, she was trying to dance outside the edges of what that band would do, and now, with this latest one and its subsequent tours, she isn’t afraid to keep it intensely personal but also take it bigger and broader, without worrying whether it steps on the toes of her other gig by getting too raucous, or too rock.

	Not to negate the other thing, which you get the feeling could come back in a couple of years, or never, or some time in between. You can believe that the stuff she’s doing now is as good as she’s gotten, and still think it’d be fun to see Paramore reconvene and play the Bowl, too, some time down the road. Right now, anyway, it’s Hayley Williams’ bachelorette party, and the favors are tremendous.

title: Disney Cruise Ship Believe to Debut ‘Encanto’ Musical, ‘Frozen’ Family Feast and More
description: Disney has unveiled its latest cruise ship, Believe. The ship will embark on its maiden voyage on Dec. 18, 2027 from its homeport of Port Everglades
body:
Disney has unveiled its latest cruise ship, Believe. The ship will embark on its maiden voyage on Dec. 18, 2027 from its homeport of Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

	Among the brand-new experiences is the first stage adaptation of “Disney Encanto,” which will premiere on board and is being developed exclusively for the Disney Believe.

	“Oaken’s Table: A Frozen Family Feast,” a brand-new, untold chapter in the “Frozen” story featuring Oaken, Anna and Kristoff, will also be unveiled. Set in a courtyard deep within the forest, Oaken and his family will invite guests to dine together while enjoying the musical stylings of his cousins.
	



	

	



	Guests can also experience The Grand Hall, a living theater where characters from across the Disney universe take center stage, designed to evoke the vibrant world where the sky meets the sea from Disney Animation’s “Moana” films.


	Among the other entertainment experiences based on Disney IP, the Wishing Well is a gathering space themed to the iconic settings and locales featured in the Disney animated classic “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.” Gazelle will be a “Zootopia”-inspired entertainment hub offering a variety of live shows designed for families to laugh, sing and compete together (plus adult-exclusive options at night). Inside Out: Joyful Sweets offers confectionery inspired by the Pixar series’ expanded cast of emotions from “Inside Out 2.” And there will be new cafes themed to “Big Hero 6″ and “Moana.”



	

	



	Disney Believe joins its sister ships Disney Wish, Disney Treasure and Disney Destiny. It is part of the growth plan for Disney Cruise Line which will see the fleet expand to 13 ships in late 2030.

schema.headline: Disney Cruise Ship Believe to Debut ‘Encanto’ Musical, ‘Frozen’ Family Feast and More

title: ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to ‘Yellowstone’ Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’
description: Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylo
body:
Kevin Costner and Luke Grimes may have played a father-son duo on-screen in “Yellowstone,” but off-screen, the two actors haven’t spoken since Taylor Sheridan’s Western drama concluded.

	“I’ve never spoken to Kevin since we stopped working together,” Grimes, who now stars in the “Yellowstone” spin-off “Marshals,” said in a recent interview with USA Today. “Not for any other reason other than just, you know, we’re both busy guys and life moves on.”
	

	“Yellowstone” ran for five seasons and came to an end in December, 2024. Costner appeared as the family patriarch, John Dutton, while Grimes played John’s youngest son, Kayce. Grimes appeared on the show throughout the duration of its run, while Costner’s character was killed off and subsequently did not return for the final six episodes of the show that made up Season 5B.


	When asked if Costner would make a future appearance in “Marshals,” the actor said it “would be cool,” though he noted, “I doubt that will happen at this point.” He continued: “I just don’t know… I think, if there was a flashback, I’d probably rather it be with Monica than John. I think that’d be more poignant to the character, but we’ll see.” (Grimes was referring to Monica Long Dutton, Kayce’s wife, played by Kelsey Asbille. Her character has died of cancer by the time “Marshals” premieres.)

	“I think that’d be more poignant to the character,” he said. “There’s been no conversation, but I sure would love it. I love working with her.”

	Per the official “Marshals” logline, the spin-off follows Kayce as he ventures beyond Yellowstone Ranch and joins an “elite unit of U.S. Marshals, combining his skills as a cowboy and Navy SEAL to bring range justice to Montana, where he and his teammates must balance family, duty and the high psychological cost that comes with serving as the last line of defense in the region’s war on violence.”
	

	Season 1 of the show premiered earlier this year in March, while Season 2 premiered Sunday.

title: Payal Kapadia, Anurag Kashyap Joined by Kavita Gupta’s Cineroost as Producer on Prateek Vats’ ‘Chronicles of a Confession’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and A
body:
Kavita Gupta’s U.S.-based Cineroost has boarded Prateek Vats’ second feature, “Chronicles of a Confession,” as producer, joining Payal Kapadia and Anurag Kashyap on the project, which starts shooting in early November.

	Cineroost stepped in to handle global representation and U.S. markets, and to help get the film into production. It is the company’s next feature after Vir Das’ “Baara Number.”


	Written by Vidur Nauriyal, Vats and Shubham, the drama centers on a shawl seller who admits to a crime he didn’t commit, kicking off a series of events nobody saw coming. The script was chosen for the Busan International Film Festival‘s Asian Cinema Fund, under its script development strand.
	

	Vats broke through with “Eeb Allay Ooo!,” which world premiered at the Pingyao Film Festival in 2019 and took the Golden Gateway award at the Mumbai Film Festival that year. The film went on to screen at the Berlinale in 2020 and at Tribeca’s first online edition.


	Ranjan Singh of Flip Films (“Songs of Forgotten Trees,” “Vagachipaani”) produces alongside Dubai’s Action Filmz, India’s Etched Films and Khan & Kumar Productions (“Lovers in the Blue Night”). The project’s producing and creative base stretches across India, the U.S. and the U.A.E. Kashyap and Kapadia serve as executive producers.

	Kashyap, who was involved in Vats’ first film, said the director had spent a long time on a script he envies. “I almost want to steal it. And since I can’t, I have jumped on board as an executive producer,” Kashyap said. “It is an honor to associate with someone as great as Payal Kapadia who I have seen sticking to her voice and her ground as a filmmaker and then there is my own producer Ranjan Singh. What was there in this to not want to be part of it.”
	

	Anand Bansal (“Dhuin,” “Gamak Ghar,” “The Elephant Whisperers”) is behind the camera, with Rajesh Thanickan (“Santosh,” “Homebound”) as supervising producer. Devika Dave (“Boong,” “Sherni”) handles production design, Himani Dehlvi (“Trial by Fire”) costumes and Bigyna Dahal (“The Fable,” “Khauff”) sound design.

	“Prateek’s films mix humor and political commentary in a unique way which I have always admired. And this new project takes this to an even higher level,” Kapadia said.

	“‘Chronicles of a Confession’ has been brewing for some years and I am thrilled that it is going on floor now,” Vats said. “The film solidifies my collaboration with producer Ranjan Singh, who has been with me since my debut feature, ‘Eeb Allay Ooo!'”

	Gupta’s earliest film projects, 13 years ago, were with Kashyap, and the two have remained close. “Strong writing, the best creators and a stellar global creative team, everything about this film aligned with my vision for Cineroost – rare, global and rooted,” Gupta said.

	The film marks the second major step in building out Cineroost’s slate.

	“Business from films is not for my sustenance but really for my soul and passion,” Gupta said. “I find that to be a strength in the work I do in the creative world. I have the privilege of flirting with risk more than others.”

	“A lot of my work for South Asian talent and projects has been under the radar,” she added. “I felt time has come for me to take bigger steps and come out from being in the shadows to do what I love, nurturing creative voices, enabling stories that matter and building bridges between divergent worlds.”

schema.headline: Payal Kapadia, Anurag Kashyap Joined by Kavita Gupta’s Cineroost as Producer on Prateek Vats’ ‘Chronicles of a Confession’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Texas Executes Inmate After Christa Pike Survives Botched Lethal Injection
description:
Texas Inmate
                          Executed Days After Christa Pike's Botched Execution
body:
Texas Inmate
                          Executed Days After Christa Pike's Botched Execution
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 7, 2026
                            7:29 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Texas has carried out an execution days after Tennessee inmate Christa Pike survived two doses of lethal injection ... with the condemned killer's final words directed at his victim's family.
      
    
            Jamaal Howard was pronounced dead Wednesday night at a Texas prison after receiving a dose of pentobarbital ... the same drug used during Pike's botched execution last week.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Howard was convicted of fatally shooting convenience store clerk Vickie Swartout during a 2000 robbery in Texas. Surveillance video showed Howard shooting Swartout in the chest before stealing $114 and a carton of cigarettes.
      
    
            Before the execution, Howard apologized to Swartout's family, who watched from a viewing room near the death chamber.
      

            "I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness," Howard said. "I'm sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days.”"
      
    
            Howard's attorneys had asked courts to halt the execution, arguing Texas' supply of pentobarbital could be degraded and pose risks similar to those allegedly involved in Pike's failed execution.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital during her September 30 execution in Tennessee ... her attorney says they believed she was brain dead Monday night, only for her to unexpectedly wake up and begin speaking. Her lawyers blame blown veins, deteriorated drugs and a lack of emergency medical care, while Gov. Bill Lee has halted the state’s remaining execution for the year.
      
    
            As the drug took effect Wednesday, Howard gasped, coughed and made snoring sounds before all movement stopped. He was pronounced dead 19 minutes later.

description:
AZ Congressional Candidate

body:
AZ Congressional Candidate
                          I Was Raped While Campaigning
                          ... Shares Graphic Details
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 7, 2026
                            6:01 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Bernadette Greene-Placentia says she was raped in a parking lot while trying to repair a damaged campaign sign ... and she's now revealing disturbing details about the alleged attack.
      
    
            The Democratic candidate for Arizona’s 8th Congressional District told the Phoenix New Times she was assaulted around 2 AM August 14 in Sun City, a retirement community northwest of Phoenix.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Bernadette claims she was hit in the head and briefly lost consciousness. When she woke up, she says a man was on top of her and allegedly sexually assaulting her.
      

            She claims she felt a sharp pain below her waist and saw the man pulling his penis out. Bernadette says the man called her a "bitch" and told her she was "not a very good f***."
      
    
            She says a second man then approached and tried pushing her legs farther apart. Bernadette claims she began kicking at him, prompting him to say ... "Not even worth it."
      
    
            She says the men then left her face down in the parking lot. Bernadette was able to drive herself home, but says she remembers very little about what happened afterward.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            "It's just these little tiny flashes of things that I do remember," she told the outlet. "As much as I don't want to remember, I've tried very, very hard to remember more stuff. But that's where I'm at."
      
    
            The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office confirmed Bernadette filed a report August 31 and said the investigation is ongoing.
      
    
            Bernadette says she initially felt embarrassed and wanted to forget the alleged assault but decided to speak publicly because her campaign focuses on supporting sexual assault survivors.

title: CoolKicks Inc. Sues Complex, Nice Kicks For Defamation
description:
CoolKicks Inc.
                          Sues Complex For Defamation ...
body:
CoolKicks Inc.
                          Sues Complex For Defamation ...
                          Our Sneakers Aren't Counterfeit!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            CoolKicks Inc. and the company's owner, Adeel Shams, are kicking off a legal dispute with Complex and Nice Kicks ... suing the companies for defamation.
      
    
            In the lawsuit -- obtained by TMZ -- CoolKicks and Adeel say Complex published an article last year titled "Cool Kicks Raided and Accused of Selling Counterfeit Shoes" that claimed the company had been caught in a counterfeit sneaker scandal.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            CoolKicks and Adeel say the story is demonstrably false ... pointing out that law enforcement did not accuse the company or shows of selling counterfeit or fake goods.
      

            CoolKicks also claims Nice Kicks shared a social media video which likewise falsely asserted Shams was arrested and the company made fake sneakers.
      
    
            The plaintiffs say their reputations have been irrevocably damaged by the allegations ... which has proved devastating for the business in turn.
      
    
            CoolKicks and Adeel claim Complex has refused to print a retraction ... and, now, they say it's too late to undo the previous damage.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Complex and Nice Kicks are being sued for defamation, trade libel, and false light.
      
    
            We've reached out to Complex for comment ... so far, no word back.

title: Cornell Rape Case Defendant's Lawyer Moves to Block Letitia James From Running Investigation
description:
Accused Cornell Frat Bro's Lawyer
                          Wants Judge to Prevent Letitia James
body:
Accused Cornell Frat Bro's Lawyer
                          Wants Judge to Prevent Letitia James From Running Investigation
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            An attorney for one of the men accused in the Cornell 7 rape case is asking a judge to officially block New York Attorney General Letitia James from running the criminal investigation ... claiming her public comments create an appearance of bias.
      
    
            Gillio Lopes' ttorneys filed a petition Wednesday, asking the court to void Governor Kathy Hochul's appointment of James as special prosecutor or limit her personal involvement in the case.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            According to court docs obtained by TMZ, James posted on the New York Attorney General's official social media September 28 ... just a few days before her appointment saying the alleged victim's experience was "horrific and unacceptable" and that she stood with her and "all survivors."
      

            Lopes' attorneys argue the statement suggests James may have formed an opinion about the allegations before being swith investigating them.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The petition acknowledges James later said her office would conduct the investigation "fully and fairly" and be guided by the facts and the law. However, Lopes' lawyers claim the assurance does not erase concerns raised by her earlier comments.
      
    
            "This is neither personal nor political. It is about the integrity of the investigative process," the petition says.
      
    
            The petition does not seek to stop the investigation. Instead, Lopes' attorneys want James' appointment voided and a new special prosecutor appointed without any actual or perceived bias against Lopes or the other accused fraternity members.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we've previously reported, a former Cornell student sued the university, Chi Phi and seven former fraternity members, including Lopes, alleging she was drugged and sexually assaulted by multiple men at the school's Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.
      
    
            New York's Govener later issued an executive order assigning James' office control of the investigation and any potential prosecution.
